### MEDIUM: Docs weaken the serving\-authorization precondition and diverge from the repo's own policy reference
[docs/architecture/security/attestation\.md:106](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/ca7f5751bb19081015146fee75944749bb40cd8e/docs/architecture/security/attestation.md#L106) · A-016, T-052, T-053, T-055, TB-011

The rewritten Context paragraph says missing receipt/risk evidence "does not clear an accepted, otherwise valid basic grant"\. Receipt/risk checks now apply only to rewards and MDM\-removal readiness, and the page points to an external platform commit\. The base text, and the unchanged line 10 and line 19 of this page, still defer to the in\-repo reference/provider\-authorization\.md\. That reference required a verified current risk receipt and complete metric before any grant\. The architecture docs now disagree with each other and the canonical threat model \(TB\-011, T\-052, T\-053, T\-055\)\. Reviewers and operators cannot tell whether a provider with an unverified or missing receipt can serve public traffic\. If this describes real behavior, the receipt gate is no longer a serving control: a provider whose receipt lapses, or one that never obtains a risk metric, keeps serving until the proof or policy deadline\. Fix: update the threat model and in\-repo provider\-authorization\.md together, state which revision is authoritative, and record the receipt\-gating change as a residual risk in T\-052/T\-053/T\-055\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

### MEDIUM: Endpoint\-resumption custody response is new attack surface not covered by the threat model
[docs/architecture/components/provider\.md:74](https://github.com/Layr-Labs/d-inference/blob/ca7f5751bb19081015146fee75944749bb40cd8e/docs/architecture/components/provider.md#L74) · A-003, A-016, T-053, T-054, TB-002, TB-011

The new protocol\-1 endpoint\-custody response answers a coordinator\-supplied nonce inside CoordinatorClient, using the process X25519 key\. It does no Apple work\. Docs say a matching platform can combine it with retained evidence to resume authorization after a same\-process reconnect\. Nothing in TB\-002, TB\-011, T\-053 or A\-003 covers this path\. Risks: \- Custody of the X25519 key does not by itself prove Apple App Attest credential, build or SIP state\. A replaced or modified process, or a compromised or colluding operator, could resume a grant without a fresh assertion\. \- The key becomes a response oracle for any nonce the coordinator sends\. The domain separation and origin binding are not shown\. \- Resumption could extend effective authorization beyond the original proof validity if the platform implementation is wrong\. The docs only say the platform "must preserve original proof deadlines" and re\-check revocation, so this is an unenforced assumption\. Fix: add the threat and its mitigations to the model \(domain\-separated nonce, binding to connection, endpoint and policy generation, no lifetime extension, revocation checked at resume and at every final handoff\)\. Add a coordinator\-side test\.

Raised by: anthropic/claude\-sonnet\-5\.5

findings.detail: The replaced paragraph defers to an external darkbloom-platform contract. It says missing receipt or risk evidence "alone does not clear an accepted, otherwise valid basic grant" and that only reward and MDM-removal readiness are withheld. The canonical model (TB-011, T-053, T-057) and the removed base text require a fresh verified risk receipt with a complete metric for every serving grant. If the coordinator follows the new text, a credential with unverified or absent receipt evidence stays routable, and receipt monitoring stops being a serving gate. A provider could then withhold or fail receipt renewal and keep serving. The threat model has no entry for "basic grant" versus "reward-ready" authorization. Its mitigations for A-016, T-053 and T-057 should be updated or the docs corrected. The in-repo link to provider-authorization.md was also replaced by a pinned external-repo URL that this PR cannot verify. Fix: reconcile the threat model and its source-of-truth reference, and state which policy this repo's coordinator enforces.
